name: What size addition can you build before it becomes a major permit project?

mainEntity.name: What size addition becomes a major permit project in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What size addition becomes a major permit project in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A permit project becomes more complex when the addition changes the home’s structure or creates new living area, not just when it exceeds a certain square footage. A small bump-out may still require full plan review if it changes load-bearing walls, roof framing, or utility systems. Larger additions almost always bring more detailed submittals, engineering, and inspections. In Los Angeles-area jurisdictions, a project’s complexity often increases when it includes a bedroom, bathroom, kitchen expansion, or second story. Those features tend to trigger building, plumbing, electrical, mechanical, and energy documentation requirements. The lot, zoning, and existing house condition can also affect review difficulty. Homeowners should ask early whether the project can be treated as a simple addition or whether it will require a full plan-check package. That distinction affects the budget, design timeline, and contractor selection. The earlier a project is classified correctly, the less likely it is to hit delays later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Even small additions can become major permit projects if they add habitable space, change the roofline, or affect structural, plumbing, electrical, or HVAC systems. The size alone matters less than whether the work changes the home’s structure or use.
